title: The Child in the Grave

full_text:
A heartbroken mother wept inconsolably upon the grave of her four-year-old boy. She refused all comfort from her husband and other children, spending bitter winter nights weeping upon the frozen sod.

One night, the earth opened beneath her, and she descended into the spirit realm of the churchyard.

There she found her little boy; but he was weeping bitterly! His white shroud was soaked through and heavy with her tears: "Mother! Your weeping holds me in the damp earth! I cannot fly to heaven while your sorrow binds me to the grave!"

The mother awoke with a gasp. She fell upon her knees and prayed: "Forgive my selfish grief, O Lord! Take my child into Thy peace, and teach me to love those who still live on earth."

She returned home, embraced her living children, and found peace in the sacred hope of eternity.
moral: Unrestrained grief anchors the soul to dust; faith sees the departed living in divine light.
